title: GOOD
date: Reviewed in the United States on February 13, 2026
review: The Sticky Fly Trap Indoor Hanging is a simple and reliable way to reduce annoying flies and small flying insects inside your home. Just hang it where you see activity — near windows, doors, or kitchens — and the sticky surface does the rest. No sprays, poisons, or complicated setup required.It catches flies quickly and silently, and the hanging design keeps it out of the way yet visible where it’s needed most. The traps are lightweight and easy to replace when full.Pros: Easy to use, chemical‑free, effective on common house fliesCons: Needs replacement over time, works best as part of regular pest controlBottom Line: A convenient and affordable indoor fly trap that helps keep flying insects under control without fuss — ideal for kitchens, patios, and living spaces.

title: Cheap and effective, if you have a place to hang it.
date: Reviewed in the United States on August 2, 2025
review: It's a strip of glue. If you've never used such a thing before, then this seems like an ineffective way to catch flies, but if you leave it alone for any period of time, you'll be surprised by what you find stuck to it when you come back. I don't know if it's "sufficiently" sticky, but I have multiple traps practically encrusted with flies so whatever it is, it is sticky enough. The big problem is that there are places I have an infestation but no place to attach it to; light fixtures seem best since flies like the light and will happily fly right into the trap but if you have no such place then you'll need alternate solutions.I'd take a half star away from the review if I could for that particular issue, as well as the fact that, well, it makes no bones about the fact it's basically a length of packing tape flapping in the wind and you'll be greeted with a strip of fly corpses whenever you enter a room which might be a little off-putting to say the least.  I'd probably also not use this for anything save a plague of flies, the stray fly that might find in an otherwise bug-free home probably should be dealt with in a more manual method.

title: Super sticky!  A good price
date: Reviewed in the United States on April 7, 2026
review: Very, VERY, sticky!  I ruined the first one and it ended up stuck to me and breaking - so be very careful twisting it out of the tube, don't let it touch anything!  Had to use dish liquid to get it off my skin.  So far it is catching gnats, so I may put one in the kitchen as well as the bathroom - it did not catch the huge flys that were getting in, I think they laughed at it, but if they did touch it I have no doubt it would have caught them.

title: I think it works
date: Reviewed in the United States on April 8, 2023
review: Long story short, this solved our gnat problem but I have no idea how. I don't know if anything got stuck to the tape but the bugs are gone. Since it worked, I won't question it.So we had these annoying gnats/fruit fly like bugs that were only in our bedroom for the most part. There was only like 1 or 2 per day but they were those ones that drives you nuts by flying right in your face and you can never kill them, so we bought these.They opened fairly easily without much force or the string or anything breaking randomly. I took the time to unravel it and tried pulling it tight and holding it like that for a bit, but as soon as I let go then it just wound right back up. I figured it would unravel on its own after hanging it up, so it wasn't a big deal. (The pic with more light shows how it was out of the box the first night)We put it into our ceiling above our computer where those things managed to evoke the most rage in us and went to bed. The very next morning we didn't see any flies. I didn't notice any stuck on the tape either though.Its now been 4 days since putting the fly paper up and we have not seen a single one of those gnats anywhere in my home. I *think* one may be stuck to the paper, but not completely sure, it could be dust too. I really don't understand it. We had these flies for 3 weeks and no severe change in weather or anything else, so I know it was these papers. They're the only change we made.Also side note, it ended up unraveling a little bit after we turned on our humidifier last night, but otherwise it still hasnt really straightened out yet.(You can see in the 2nd pic, the darker one where more of the window is in the shot) Its only been up for 4 days and I just measured it to be about 2 feet, even with it still curled a bit. I saw some other reviewers not like that it didnt unravel completely. I don't mind since it's not like we need the extra tape space and I'd probably manage to hit my head off it somehow if it was longer, which I'm definitely okay with never doing (again).Ultimately we bought this to get rid of our gnat problem, which it did. Even if it wasn't in the expected way. So I'm competely happy with the purchase. And it does seem sticky enough that if they land on it they would get stuck to it. Also getting 8 of them for the price is worth it as well.

title: They work great, ribbon stays sticky even months later
date: Reviewed in the United States on April 16, 2026
review: They last a super long time and overall the product does what it’s supposed to. Just wish it was easier to setup; taking the metal tack out, you have to wrap the plastic string a few times around it to secure it before you try to hang it up (I was pushing the tack in the ceiling directly) otherwise the ribbon will just slide right off it after you push it in. This just sucks because it’s almost impossible not to get the sticky goo on your fingers since the tack is not automatically wrapped with it.Also I have dropped and lost some of these tacks while attempting to hang them up and still walk around in fear of stepping on them lol
